cli.help:
Musa CAD -- 2D CAD engine

Usage:
  musacad [<drawing>]              open a drawing in the GUI
  musacad --check <drawing> [check options]
                                   read a drawing, check its text, report, exit
  musacad --plot <drawing> <out.pdf> [plot options]
                                   plot to PDF headlessly (no display needed)
  musacad --dump-wiki-data <out.json>
                                   write the commands, ribbon and keyboard
                                   shortcuts as JSON, for the documentation
  musacad --help                   show this help
  musacad --version                show the version

<drawing> is a .musa file, or a .dxf file (loaded through the DXF importer).

Plot options:
  --paper <name>    sheet: A4 A3 A2 A1 A0 Letter Tabloid   (default A4)
  --landscape       sheet orientation                      (default)
  --portrait        sheet orientation
  --extents         plot the drawing's extents             (default)
  --window x0,y0,x1,y1   plot an explicit world rectangle
  --fit             scale the area to fill the sheet       (default)
  --scale <n:m>     plot n mm per m drawing units, e.g. 1:5
  --monochrome      plot everything black (the mono CTB style)

Check options:
  --window x0,y0,x1,y1   the frame text must stay inside (default: the
                    drawing's largest rectangle)
  --lines           also report text that a line crosses
  --json            print the report as JSON

Exit codes:
  0  success
  1  usage error (bad command line)
  2  the drawing could not be read or parsed
  3  the output could not be written
  4  --check: text overlaps text, leaves the frame, crosses a line (--lines)
     or uses a character the font has no glyph for

Single-dash options are passed through to Qt (e.g. -platform offscreen).

shortcuts.description: OSNAP (F3) Snap the cursor to precise points on existing objects (endpoint, midpoint, center, ...).
ORTHO (F8) Constrain cursor movement to horizontal and vertical.
SNAP (F9) Snap the cursor to grid increments.
POLAR (F10) Track the cursor along the polar angles (the dropdown sets the increment).
OTRACK (F11) Track the cursor along paths through the object snap points it has rested on.
DYN (F12) Show command input and prompts at the cursor (Dynamic Input).
3DOSNAP (F4) Snap to the vertices, edges and faces of 3D objects.
DUCS (F6) Align the UCS with the face of a solid under the cursor (Dynamic UCS).
